title: Weekly blend quantization ops sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8/FP8 blend results, surface quality deltas, discuss latency/throughput tradeoffs and decide next tuning jobs for a broader test matrix.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, we'll give folks a minute to pop in.
[00:16] Evan Brooks: hey hey, looks like we've got everyone.
[00:18] Diego Ruiz: cool, quick agenda — results recap, open anomalies, tuning proposals, and next steps.
[00:27] Tom Hargreaves: yep that's fine. we mostly want to see if the quality regression is material for home feed ranking.
[00:34] Priya Shah: and from infra side, confirm the latency SLOs are still safe under burst.
[00:39] Maya Chen: perfect. quick note — recordings and the benchmark spreadsheet are in the shared drive, link in the calendar invite.
[00:46] Diego Ruiz: ok jumping in, slide 1 of the runbook — we ran the blend experiment where 60% of requests hit INT8 mixed-quant variant, 30% hit FP8 blend, and 10% control full-fp32. sequence lengths sampled from production trace, median 128 tokens.
[01:10] Evan Brooks: can you remind us the exact hardware?
[01:12] Diego Ruiz: yeah, tests ran on our dedicated gpus (A800 equivalent) in the staging cluster. batch sizes were auto-batched by runtime with max batch 32, and we used our KV cache warmup for conversational prefix.
[01:25] Nora Patel: important — we disabled some of the runtime micro-optimizations for parity to reduce variance.
[01:31] Tom Hargreaves: got it. so results?
[01:34] Diego Ruiz: summarized in the sheet — overall token cost decreased ~41% for INT8 path vs control and ~27% for FP8. Latency p50 improved 18% INT8, 10% FP8. p95 tail improved ~8% INT8, ~4% FP8. throughput measured in tokens/sec increased accordingly.
[01:55] Evan Brooks: those numbers look great, but we saw some quality delta on our rerank eval set — about 2.6% drop on NDCG for INT8 on long-form prompts.
[02:07] Maya Chen: yep that's the main tradeoff. can you walk us through the error modes?
[02:12] Evan Brooks: sure, two clusters — hallucination-like factual mistakes at longer contexts, and occasional truncation of entities in generated snippets. it's not uniform, seems correlated with sequence length > 512 and certain prompt templates.
[02:27] Diego Ruiz: interesting — our sensitivity graphs show divergence starting at sequence lengths around 480 tokens, so that aligns. we suspected quantization is amplifying numeric drift for key layers.
[02:38] Priya Shah: from infra, during the runs we saw a couple short CPU-side spikes when swapping KV cache segments, but they didn't correlate with the regression windows.
[02:48] Nora Patel: we also logged logits variance — for INT8 variants the logits distribution had heavier tails during those failure cases. there was also a pattern with prompt temperature — higher sampling temps increased observed delta.
[03:03] Tom Hargreaves: ok so are there immediate mitigations?
[03:06] Diego Ruiz: yes a handful: 1) limit INT8 to sequences < 400 tokens and route longer ones to FP8 or fp32; 2) increase calibration steps for specific layers (we identified 3 candidate transformer blocks); 3) tune KV cache warmup more aggressively for long contexts; 4) apply bias-correction post-quantization for top-k logits.
[03:29] Evan Brooks: we'd prefer automatic routing so we don't have to change client prompts. can the runtime route by sequence length or by a quick fidelity probe?
[03:36] Diego Ruiz: runtime supports policy-based routing — we can add a length-based rule today, and a tiny quick-probe call (100 tokens) would also work though it adds an extra hop.
[03:45] Priya Shah: concern — probe calls add cost and extra latency for first request. we might prefer a probabilistic routing that backs off for long tails.
[03:54] Maya Chen: noted. Diego, you had some micro-batching tweaks you wanted to try?
[03:58] Diego Ruiz: yeah, propose smaller max-batch for long-context buckets to reduce KV thrash, and a slightly higher concurrency cap for FP8 nodes so long requests don't pile. That reduces p95 for long requests by about 60-80ms in our internal sim.
[04:15] Evan Brooks: what's the impact on cost?
[04:18] Diego Ruiz: the higher FP8 concurrency bumps unit cost ~4-6% but keeps quality in-line, overall blended cost still down ~22% vs all-fp32 baseline.
[04:28] Tom Hargreaves: can we run a focused sensitivity sweep next week to quantify NDCG vs sequence-length and temp?
[04:34] Maya Chen: absolutely — propose a matrix: lengths [128, 256, 512, 768], temps [0.0, 0.7, 1.2], routing policy [all-int8, length-cutoff, runtime-probe, fp8-blend]. we can prioritize rows based on your production distribution.
[04:55] Evan Brooks: prioritize 256 and 512 first — most users fall there.
[04:58] Nora Patel: I'll run per-layer calibration experiments in parallel and push logs to the shared bucket. we may need to increase calibration dataset size by 30% for stability.
[05:09] Priya Shah: how long will these runs take?
[05:12] Diego Ruiz: single sweep (~4 configs) should finish in ~6 hours on the staging cluster; full matrix maybe 24-36 hours depending on queue.
[05:20] Tom Hargreaves: ok. any surprising anomalies?
[05:22] Diego Ruiz: a small subset of prompts (about 0.4% of test set) had catastrophic failures in INT8 — outputs repeated tokens or collapsed. we traced those to a specific attention head that loses dynamic range under quant.
[05:36] Nora Patel: that head is candidate for per-head higher precision— we can keep it as FP8 while quantizing the rest.
[05:42] Evan Brooks: is that supported by your compilers? runtime?
[05:44] Diego Ruiz: yes, we can do mixed-precision on a per-layer or per-head basis. it's a config flag and we can push that variant into the blend as a canary.
[05:52] Maya Chen: any legal/security concerns surfaced during the POC?
[05:55] Priya Shah: nothing new; data residency controls are intact; you shared SOC2 docs last week which helped review.
[06:02] Tom Hargreaves: from product — assuming we can get NDCG within 1% of baseline across prioritized lengths, we can move to a small pilot in prod.
[06:12] Evan Brooks: what about A/B buckets and rollback?
[06:15] Diego Ruiz: rollout plan — start with 5% traffic blend, monitor NDCG and latency telemetry, automatic fallback if NDCG drops >1.5% sustained for 30m or if error rate spikes.
[06:30] Priya Shah: also please include an SLO alert that triggers if p95 latency increases by >200ms for two consecutive 10m windows.
[06:40] Nora Patel: we'll add more instrumentation — layer-level histograms and logits variance monitors.
[06:46] Tom Hargreaves: good. can you summarize the immediate next actions?
[06:50] Maya Chen: yeah i'll recap then we'll capture action owners.
[06:53] Diego Ruiz: short term: run the prioritized sensitivity sweep (256/512 x temps) with length-based routing and per-head higher-precision variant; push per-layer calibration increases; run canary with 5% traffic after internal validation.
[07:06] Evan Brooks: for us — we'll share a curated prompt set (edge cases) and the production distribution file.
[07:12] Priya Shah: infra will schedule the staging compute and confirm quotas.
[07:16] Tom Hargreaves: product will define the acceptance criteria for the A/B (NDCG threshold + no user-visible degradation).
[07:22] Maya Chen: perfect. any blockers?
[07:25] Evan Brooks: none immediate; just want the sensitivity sweep results by next Wed.
[07:28] Nora Patel: doable.
[07:30] Diego Ruiz: i'll start the sweep tomorrow morning and share raw logs.
[07:34] Maya Chen: outstanding, let's call out action items. Thanks everyone.
[07:39] [end of call]
next_steps: Diego to run prioritized sensitivity sweep (256 & 512 lengths x temps 0.0/0.7/1.2) and share results by 2026-02-24
Nora to increase calibration dataset by 30% and run per-layer calibration experiments; upload logs to shared bucket by 2026-02-23
Evan to provide curated edge-case prompt set and production distribution file by 2026-02-19
